# Counterexample to the proposed global exclusive-volume bound

The proposed statement was: in continuous dimension d=2, a strict minimal
cover by k<=3m equal-mass caps, m=2^n, with common normalized cap mass

  tau < 1/(2m)

satisfies E <= (3/2)m tau M, where E is the measure of points covered by
exactly one open cap and M is the total mixed volume. The statement is false,
including strict minimality and the allowed case k<3m.

## The convex body and its two fibers

Take n=1, d=2, m=2. Use coordinates (z,x,y). Put

  A=115/243, B=128/243, L=256/243, tau=6/25,
  K_0=[0,A] x [0,1],
  K_1=conv{(0,0),(L,0),(0,1)},
  C=conv(({0} x K_0) union ({1} x K_1)).

The convex body C is full-dimensional and has exactly two integer fibers,
K_0 and K_1. Their areas are A and B, so M=A+B=1. In particular

  tau=6/25 < 1/4 = 1/(2m).

## Five explicit closed halfspaces

Take the following caps, using strict versions for the open cover:

  H_1: z+x <= 6/25,
  H_2: x-2z >= 115/243-6/25,
  H_3: 2z-x/L-y >= 53/40,
  H_4: 2z+x/L >= 93/40,
  H_5: 2z+y >= 93/40.

H_1 and H_2 miss the entire z=1 fiber and restrict on z=0 to
x<=tau and x>=A-tau. Each has area tau. Since A<2tau, their open interiors
cover K_0. Both are necessary: points with x near 0 belong only to H_1,
and points with x near A belong only to H_2.

H_3,H_4,H_5 miss the entire z=0 fiber. On K_1 introduce barycentric
coordinates

  lambda_0=1-x/L-y, lambda_1=x/L, lambda_2=y.

The three caps are respectively lambda_i>=13/40. Each therefore takes
(27/40)^2 of K_1's area. Their common area is exactly

  B(27/40)^2 = (128/243)(729/1600) = 6/25 = tau.

Since 3(13/40)=39/40<1, their open interiors cover all of K_1. Each is
necessary, as seen at the corresponding simplex vertex; interior witnesses
can be chosen with its barycentric coordinate 4/5 and the other two 1/10.
Thus the complete five-cap cover is strict and inclusion-minimal. All normals
have nonzero continuous components, and all boundaries have zero mixed area.

## Exact exclusive-volume calculation

The rectangle's two caps overlap in area 2tau-A, so its exclusive area is

  E_0=2A-2tau=2834/6075.

The triple overlap of the three triangle caps is a similar triangle with
area

  T=B(1-3(13/40))^2=B/1600=2/6075.

Multiplicity counting inside the triangle gives

  E_1=2B-3tau+T=2028/6075.

There are no cross-fiber cap overlaps. Consequently

  E=E_0+E_1=4862/6075,
  (3/2)m tau M = 3tau = 18/25 = 4374/6075,
  E-(3/2)m tau M = 488/6075 > 0.

All five caps have exactly the same global mass tau, and k=5<=6=3m.
This falsifies the proposed bound under tau<1/(2m).

The example does not violate OC: tau=6/25 is greater than its target
2^{-1} gamma_2=2/9. It demonstrates that the proposed wider-threshold
exclusive-volume lemma cannot be used to establish OC as stated.
